New original layout: city on a broad headland with a sweeping natural harbor on the southeast/right and lower edge, hinterland roads entering from northwest/upper-left. Dense maze of hundreds of narrow streets and rooflines in lower Waterside, quays, warehouses and numerous sailing-ship docks along harbor. Higher inland Hillside district in upper-left/upper-center, larger stone merchant houses, courtyards and broad cleaner streets, topographic hatching separating higher and lower ground; both districts WITHIN the city. A central connecting avenue and several smaller lanes make navigation clear. Five marked-by-architecture places, clearly separated: Hillside upper-left, Waterside center-lower, a small dockside tavern by the southeast quays, a distinctive connected roof cluster in poor western Waterside, a modest old building with visible external cellar steps beside a cramped western Waterside alley for Trapis's Cellar. These five should have labels 'Hillside', 'Waterside', 'Dockside Tavern', 'Rooftops', "Trapis's Cellar". Sea label 'The Reft'. Title 'Tarbean'. No river bisecting the city, no invented Omphalos River, cathedral name, named bridge, or other towns. Never use earlier Tarbean maps: only this new geographic brief.
